gen_risks.description: Weak strategic planning and policy coordination across participating line ministries may lead to implementation deficits in competitiveness and jobs reforms.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish an inter-ministerial Policy Planning, Monitoring, and Coordination (PPMC) Working Group led by the Public Policy Secretariat to oversee performance targets and M&E.
gen_risks.evidence: recognizing that weak planning and implementation deficits are among the most significant risks to the reform program.

gen_risks.description: Implementing agencies (PPS, MoE, MoLEVSA) lack experience with World Bank procurement and fiduciary procedures, risking procurement delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire experienced procurement and financial management specialists within PPS and MoLEVSA, and conduct intensive procurement training.
gen_risks.evidence: most of the entities involved in project implementation, have no experience in implementing World Bank-funded projects and with Bank procurement

gen_risks.description: Subordinated development agencies under the Ministry of Economy have overlapping mandates and non-transparent programs, leading to inefficient public spending.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt and execute a costed strategic framework and action plan to restructure MoE agencies (SIEPA, Development Fund, AOFI, NARR) and establish clear KPIs.
gen_risks.evidence: The system of support provided by the MoE’s agencies is complex and non-transparent.

gen_risks.description: Sub-projects financed under the Innovation Fund's Mini and Matching Grants programs may generate adverse physical environmental impacts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply an Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF) requiring sub-project screening, EMPs, and explicit exclusion of Category A activities.
gen_risks.evidence: Direct, physical environmental impacts could arise under Component 2 on Innovation... The main environmental concern deals with the Mini & Matching Grant Programs

gen_risks.description: High effective tax rates and dollar-for-dollar social benefit reductions penalize social assistance recipients who transition into formal employment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Design and pilot an in-work conditional cash transfer program to reduce effective tax rates and strengthen formal work incentives.
gen_risks.evidence: This combination makes low-paying work unviable in the formal sector.

gen_risks.description: Extreme variations in caseloads per caseworker across National Employment Service branch offices undermine job search counseling and employer outreach.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt staffing reforms to rebalance caseload dispersion across offices, reassign administrative staff, and separate inactive jobseekers into a dedicated registry.
gen_risks.evidence: average caseload varies between around 200 to over 2,000 registered unemployed per case worker across branch offices

gen_risks.description: Enterprise innovation matching grant programs face suspension if state budget allocations are not secured following the deployment of EU IPA pilot funds.
gen_risks.mitigation: Tie loan disbursements under DLI 3 directly to mandatory annual state budget allocations for Innovation Fund operating costs and matching grant budgets.
gen_risks.evidence: IF could not launch a new call for proposals in 2015.

gen_risks.description: The public research sector is disconnected from economic needs and lacks incentives for intellectual property protection and commercialization.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct RDI self-assessments and external audits by international experts, and design performance-based management and financing schemes.
gen_risks.evidence: Serbia’s public research sector suffers from the traditional post-transition malaise of being disconnected from contemporary needs and trends

gen_risks.description: Absence of technology transfer infrastructure and transactional capacity prevents academic research discoveries from reaching market readiness.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy a centralized Technology Transfer Facility at the Innovation Fund to support local TTOs and execute technology commercialization transactions.
gen_risks.evidence: absence of a functional system that could promote technology transfer within and beyond Serbia.

gen_risks.description: Economic recession and fiscal consolidation constraints may limit private investment and restrict government spending for economic programs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Structure project financing around results-based reimbursement of existing salary budget lines without expanding net government fiscal overhead.
gen_risks.evidence: The disastrous floods of May 2014 triggered a further recession. Serbia’s GDP is still below the pre-crisis level

gen_risks.description: Delays or non-achievement of Disbursement-Linked Indicators (DLIs) could lead to withheld IBRD loan reimbursements to the state budget.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize Part B technical assistance funds to support DLI execution, enable partial payments where appropriate, and allow formal reassessment requests.
gen_risks.evidence: In the event a DLI is not achieved, a 'request for reassessment' may be submitted by the Government

gen_risks.description: High perceived corruption risks in the public sector could undermine transparency in program implementation and contract awards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce strict World Bank anti-corruption guidelines, public disclosure of contract awards, and independent international peer review panels for grants.
gen_risks.evidence: Perceived level of corruption in the country is high.

gen_risks.description: Fixed minimum social security contribution floors create a high tax wedge for low-wage and part-time workers, driving employment into informality.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct technical studies to support social security contribution reform in coordination with parallel World Bank development policy lending operations.
gen_risks.evidence: This makes any formal part-time work unviable, but also makes full time work below 40 percent of average wage relatively expensive

gen_risks.description: Inadequate contract administration procedures between the PPS and line ministries may cause procurement delays and slow execution of consultancies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement dedicated contract management training, regular compliance reviews, and close procurement supervision by World Bank staff.
gen_risks.evidence: Contract administration procedures may not be adequate to ensure efficient and timely contract implementation

gt_risks.description: Program success relies on continuous, engaged commitment from the Prime Minister, Deputy PM, Minister of Finance, Minister of Education/Science/Technological Development, Minister of Labor/Employment/Veterans/Social Affairs, and the Public Policy Secretariat (PPS); line ministries must sustain interest in policy coordination or the loan will not disburse. Risk is heightened by political instability, frequent historical changes in ministers/senior staff, and excessive concentration of decision-making at the top (per the Bank's Systematic Country Diagnostic).
gt_risks.mitigation: Strong communications with the public, private sector, civil society, and EU Delegation to maintain a broad-based reform coalition; Bank coordinates communications with the PM's office; periodic PPMC Working Group consultations with private sector/civil society; ongoing close consultation with the EU Delegation in Serbia.

gt_risks.description: Significant downside macroeconomic risks: lower-than-expected Eurozone recovery could hurt Serbia's exports, remittances, and capital flows (EU countries are its largest trading partners). Materializing fiscal risks (e.g. SOE subsidy reduction difficulties) or weakening growth/currency would require even greater fiscal consolidation in 2015-2016 to keep public debt sustainable; reduced exports/FDI or greater consolidation could dampen anticipated reform impact.
gt_risks.mitigation: Bank works closely with government and the IMF to keep SOE/public-utility reform on track and ensure it generates required fiscal savings.

gt_risks.description: Project works across three ministries (MoE plus development agencies, MoESTD, MoLEVSA) plus the PPS, creating implementation complexity for both government and Bank. Achieving the DLIs requires substantial external technical assistance, but Bank supervision resources are limited and the government is reluctant to borrow for TA (would rather minimize loan-funded TA or substitute other donor resources), risking inadequate TA resourcing.
gt_risks.mitigation: Team seeks complementary resources (e.g. CIIP Trust Fund) and leverages work from other WBG projects; collaborates with other donors such as the EU and USAID.

gt_risks.description: Overall coordination sits with the Public Policy Secretariat (PPS), created only in spring 2014 under the new government; as a new institution it lacks capacity and a full set of official administrative procedures for cross-ministry policy coordination. Substantial risk to both project implementation (fiduciary/safeguards requirements, cross-ministry results reporting) and coordination of the inter-ministerial PPMC Working Group.
gt_risks.mitigation: PPS expected to hire additional personnel for fiduciary requirements and project coordination; Bank provides TA through the CIIP trust fund to strengthen PPS capacity.

gt_risks.description: PPS currently has no fiduciary experience managing Bank projects.
gt_risks.mitigation: Build capacity by establishing a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) within the PPS responsible for implementation, adequately staffing its fiduciary functions.

gt_risks.description: Reforms create both winners and losers, and losers are often more visible and organized at the time of reform (e.g. beneficiaries of MoE incentives/subsidies, National Employment Service case-workers, researchers at research institutes slated for restructuring).
gt_risks.mitigation: Government to clearly communicate reform objectives, expected outcomes, and benefits throughout the process.
